item.title: 2027 election: Makinde may succumb to Atiku; I wish he’s with us — Bwala
item.description: Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Policy Communications, Daniel Bwala, has expressed hope that Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde would join the ruling All Progressives Congress and support Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, saying he would prefer the governor to align with them rather than former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Bwala warned that Makinde would betray Southern Nigeria if he backed Atiku in the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the presidency should remain in the South for eight years. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Bwala said he believed Makinde could eventually align with Tinubu, but expressed concern over the governor’s reported political dealings with Atiku. “Seyi Makinde, I have a belief in me that at some point he would even join Asiwaju, but let’s assume he doesn’t. The people he’s leading are not stupid. Power needs to remain in the South for eight years,” he said. Bwala said Makinde’s support for Atiku would amount to a betrayal of the South, given the region’s interest in retaining the presidency beyond Tinubu’s first term. “If he is going to succumb to Atiku Abubakar, he’s betraying the people of the South,” he said. Asked why he believed Makinde might support Atiku, the presidential aide claimed the arrangement had already been agreed to in principle, adding that events would confirm his assertion. “It is already agreed in principle and you will see what I am saying,” Bwala said. He also questioned Makinde’s chances if the governor decided to contest the presidency independently, arguing that he would struggle to defeat Tinubu in Oyo State. Bwala warned that such a move could damage Makinde’s political future. “That means his political career will be dead forever. Now, let’s assume he’s going to stand on his own to become president. How can Seyi defeat Asiwaju in Oyo State?” he said. The presidential aide also ruled out the possibility of either Atiku or Peter Obi stepping down for the other ahead of the election, saying both politicians had strong commitments to their supporters. Bwala said Obi’s supporters, particularly members of the Obidient Movement, expected him to contest the presidency, arguing that withdrawing for another candidate would amount to betraying their trust. “Peter Obi is running, if you ask obedient members, they’ll say because they believe Obi himself must be the president of Nigeria. That is his legitimacy. If Peter Obi now stops running and goes to another person, he has betrayed the trust. He has betrayed the covenant,” he said. He added that Obi was unlikely to step down for another candidate. item.title: Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures
item.description: President Donald Trump called Thursday for an investigation into a routine revision of economic growth figures as he pushed his groundless claims of interference in the US midterm elections. Trump lashed out at what he called “FAKE” figures a day after the US Commerce Department strongly revised GDP growth in the third quarter up to 4.3 percent from the previous estimate of 3.4 percent. Such updates are commonplace. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error.” Trump followed up in a lengthy second post for the US Thanksgiving holiday in which he also took aim at a series of perceived enemies and critics of his extensive makeover of the White House. “I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late,” wrote Trump. He added that it was a “RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.” Trump’s allegation of deliberate action echoes his other recent baseless claims calling into doubt his Republican Party’s brutal defeat in the November 3 midterm elections. Democrats won control of Congress as voters hammered Trump’s Republicans over economic headwinds sparked by the Iran war and the president’s chaotic tariff policies. Throughout his two presidencies, the 80-year-old Trump has repeatedly attacked the political, legal and economic norms that have long underpinned US democracy. Trump has previously defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom. Issuing its new GDP estimate on Wednesday, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis said the growth “primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports.” Vanguard News The post Trump demands probe into ‘fake’ US GDP figures appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG hails Davido, Asake, others over 2027 Grammy nominations
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Federal Government has congratulated Nigerian music stars Davido, Tems, Asake, Ayra Starr, Wizkid and Burna Boy following their nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, congratulated the artistes in a post on her official X account on Thursday, describing their nominations as a source of pride for the country. Musawa noted that Nigerian artistes accounted for three of the five nominees in the Best Global Music Album category and featured in four of the five entries for Best African Music Performance. “Your music travels because it is yours. Every record also employs producers, engineers, dancers and crews, and protecting what creators own is at the heart of our work,” she wrote. She added that the country would be cheering the Nigerian nominees at the awards ceremony scheduled for February 7, 2027. The Recording Academy announced the nominees on November 16, with the six Nigerian artistes earning recognition across five categories. In the Best African Music Performance category, Asake received a nomination for his song ‘Gratitude’, while his collaboration with Wizkid, ‘Jogodo’, also made the list. Tems was nominated for ‘Big Daddy’, while Ayra Starr earned a nod alongside Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo for their collaboration, ‘Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)’. Davido, Ayra Starr and Tems also secured nominations in the Best Global Music Album category for their respective projects, ‘Oriadé’, ‘Starrgirl’ and ‘Love Is a Kingdom’. Burna Boy earned a nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category for ‘Dìá Dìá’, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira. Tems further received nominations in the Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song categories for her song ‘What You Need’. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States, on February 7, 2027. item.title: UNICEF, NGE, DAME others make case for 18.3m out-of-school children
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners have called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million out-of-school children in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. “In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, justice for survivors
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a special reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s landmark publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said although the achievement deserved celebration, sexual violence remained a difficult issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” The British envoy stressed the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, noting that their voices were essential to understanding the challenges they faced and improving access to support and justice. He said the UK remained committed to ending violence against women and girls in all its forms through development partnerships, programmes and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. Baxter disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit focusing on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches, tools and solutions. He also commended the Mirabel Centre for its pioneering work, describing it as a Nigerian organisation addressing local challenges and changing lives through its support for survivors. Earlier, Eze-Anaba said the centre’s journey could not be told without acknowledging the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission. She disclosed that the British High Commission provided funding for the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and opportunities to advocate for survivors. According to her, the achievement was not merely about the number of survivors supported but the quality, dignity and respect with which services were delivered. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors to assess its services and identify areas requiring improvement. item.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. He asked promoters of the slogan to “publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature.” “It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he said then. Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, later visited the families of the victims. Obi also spoke to Channels Television on the slogan. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die,'” he said. Obi was also reported to have said that the slogan “simply means, do not rig the election. We want a free and fair election. It never meant campaign and die.” He also defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement, who carry sticks to political gatherings. He said they have never used them to harm anyone. However, Keyamo dismissed the explanation, saying Obi’s camp was the one casting itself as the aggrieved party. “This is a classic case of the villain playing the victim,” he said. item.title: NAF: Tinubu Approves ₦100m, Houses For Families Of Air Crash Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved a monetary compensation of ₦100 million for the families of military personnel and civilians who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The President also approved a three-bedroom flat in Abuja for the families of military personnel and civilians who lost their lives in the air crash. ﻿ President Tinubu gave the approval during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony in honour of the 25 victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. In his address, the President commiserated with the bereaved families, the military and the nation, as he promised better equipment for the military. “It places upon us a sacred duty to safeguard their well-being, strengthen their capabilities and honour their service. As Commander-in-Chief, I reaffirm my administration’s commitment to a professional, well-equipped, and mission-ready Armed Forces. We will continue to prioritise modernisation, training, operational safety, and the welfare of our personnel. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wing it can build. We must also stand by the families who bear the deepest cost of national service. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of a three-bedroom flat in the Renewed Hope housing project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. No home can ever replace the one you have lost. But they gave their lives to Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their families a home. This honour is extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board,” Tinubu said. “In addition to the flats, those officers will receive from this government ₦100 million each to settle their families. I will commit their soul into the massive hands of Almighty God.” The President assured Nigerians that the accident would be thoroughly investigated, adding that his administration will strengthen the military and civilian aviation safety standards. “Your loss is our nation’s loss, and your grief is our grief. They were not merely passengers aboard the aircraft. They were our gallant officers, airmen and airwomen and fellow compatriots who travelled along with them. They were parents who will not see their children grow. They were newlyweds whose marriage and marriages had only just begun. They were sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, husbands, wives and friends,” he said. “They carried dreams in their hearts and our flag on their shoulders. We could not bring them home to you, and our inability to recover their remains has made this harder still. But hear me, the sky did not take their honour. Nothing can diminish the worth of their lives or the love they leave behind. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. item.title: 2027: Nwifuru, Umahi, Anyim rally support for Tinubu
item.description: …Umahi targets 1.3m votes, warns against hate speech By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Anyim Pius Anyim; and former Nigerian Ambassador to Greece, Chief Franklin Ogbuewu, have mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. They declared their support on Thursday during the APC’s state campaign flag-off in Afikpo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. Addressing supporters at the event, Nwifuru described the APC as a comprehensive political party with candidates for all elective positions in the state and urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other party candidates. The governor commended Tinubu for what he described as massive infrastructure development in Afikpo and urged residents to reciprocate the President’s efforts through their votes in 2027. “We are campaigning for all our candidates, beginning with the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On January 16, 2027, you will be voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What you will see on the ballot is the symbol of our great party, the broom. That broom represents the unity that has brought us together and sustained the peace we enjoy. “When you thumbprint on the broom, you have voted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On the same day, you will also vote for our senatorial candidate, Professor Anthony Okorie, a distinguished scholar and accomplished academic. “You will equally vote for our own brother, a very calm, resilient, committed and unassuming person, Elumakama Joseph, who is our House of Representatives candidate,” he said. Nwifuru appealed to political leaders and residents of Afikpo to support all APC candidates, arguing that his ability to represent the state effectively would be strengthened by Tinubu’s re-election. “I am not asking you to vote for me alone. I want you to understand that voting for me without voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will not serve our collective interest. “If you vote for me without supporting President Tinubu, I will not have the necessary political leverage to represent you effectively before him,” he said. The governor further urged residents not to take the Federal Government’s projects in the state for granted, claiming that no previous administration since independence had initiated and commissioned infrastructure projects in Ebonyi on the scale of the Tinubu administration. In his remarks, former SGF Anyim urged residents to demonstrate their support for Nwifuru by voting for Tinubu and other APC candidates. item.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. Reaffirming his administration’s position on negotiations with armed groups, the governor said: “I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals.” The post Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Saturday conduct a mock test of its voter accreditation technology in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise will take place in 406 polling units across the state’s 18 local government areas between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. INEC said the exercise was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify potential technical challenges ahead of the general elections. In a statement, the Deputy Director and Head of Department, Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, said two polling units had been selected from each of the 203 registration areas in the state. The Commission explained that the test would assess how the BVAS performs under different conditions and enable it to address any technical issues identified before the elections. INEC stressed that the exercise was not an election, adding that no voter would cast a ballot for any candidate or political party. It urged residents of the affected polling units, community leaders, political parties, civil society organisations and journalists to cooperate with its officials to ensure a successful exercise. The Commission also cautioned against the spread of rumours and fake news, urging residents to obtain election-related information only through its official communication channels. It said the mock accreditation exercise was part of its early preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of technology and the conduct of credible elections in 2027. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: Gov Okpebholo Denies Involvement In Attack On NDC Members, Obi’s Supporters
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has denied allegations linking him, the All Progressives Congress (APC), or its supporters to the alleged violent attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during the party’s activities in Benin City, the state capital. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ehor, headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, and Ekpoma in Esan West, the governor described the allegations as unfounded, insisting that neither the state government nor the APC had any reason to disrupt opposition political activities. ﻿ Okpebholo alleged that the incident involved irresponsible elements who were fighting among themselves, dismissing claims of government involvement. He said his priority remained the development of Edo State, stressing that he would not divert his attention to political violence or activities capable of undermining the progress of the state. The governor recalled that he did not engage thugs during his senatorial and governorship campaigns, alleging that a police officer was killed during the governorship election by individuals he claimed were linked to the opposition. He also vowed to sustain his administration’s crackdown on cultism and other criminal activities, insisting that elections should be conducted based on the principle of one man, one vote. Okpebholo urged residents to participate actively in the electoral process, while thanking APC supporters for their turnout at the rally. Earlier, Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa urged the people to vote for APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections, while party chairman Jarrett Tenebe commended the governor’s efforts in tackling kidnapping and cultism, urging continued support for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. Political thugs on Wednesday attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the NDC in Benin City, after the party said it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was expected to address supporters. The Edo State Coordinator of the party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, said the party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport. Videos obtained by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party convoys, including bullet casings seen on the floor of the party’s campaign office. The incident came barely 48 hours after former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy was also attacked during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, in Delta State on Monday. Last week, the Edo State Police Command commenced an investigation into an attack on the NDC secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men alleged to be members of the Edo State Security Network. item.title: 2027: Don’t Vote for Me If You Won’t Vote Tinubu, Nwifuru Tells Ebonyi Residents
item.description: The ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has officially flagged off its 2027 governorship and general election campaigns in Afikpo Local Government Area, with Governor Francis Nwifuru declaring that the party’s campaign is an all-encompassing mission aimed at securing victory for all APC flagbearers, beginning with President Bola Tinubu. ﻿ Leading the charge, Governor Nwifuru, accompanied by his deputy, Princess Patricia Obila, arrived in Afikpo to a rousing welcome from party stalwarts, stakeholders, and thousands of enthusiastic supporters ahead of the grand rally. “We are here to campaign for our party, and our party is very comprehensive,” he said while addressing the massive crowd. “We are here to campaign for all our candidates, starting with President Bola Tinubu. On the first day of the election, you will be voting for President Bola Tinubu. “Vote the broom, the symbol of unity. On that same day, vote for Senator Anthony Ani, and for the great people of Afikpo/Edda Federal Constituency, vote for Joseph Ekumankama.” In a striking display of loyalty, the governor urged Ebonyi electorate to prioritise President Tinubu’s re-election above his own second-term bid, warning that an opposition victory at the federal level would stall ongoing critical infrastructure projects in the state. “If anyone will not vote for the President, that person should not vote for me,” Nwifuru stated firmly, stressing that he would not have the moral standing to face the President if Ebonyi failed to deliver. “Voting for me is not as important as voting for the President. If the President does not win, the opposition will not complete the ongoing projects; they won’t continue them; they will abandon them,” he said. Reiterating the state’s commitment to delivering 1.3 million votes for President Tinubu, Nwifuru urged residents to resist political deception, noting that the President had rewarded Ebonyi generously despite the state giving him only 14 percent of its votes in 2023. “I am not disturbed because I know the President means well for us,” he stated. “No President has ever started and finished a major project in Ebonyi, but Tinubu has done it for us.” “He appointed our own son as the Minister of Works, giving us the biggest ministry. This time around, we owe the President. We are indebted to him for the projects in Ebonyi. Take this message home: no other person will love us the way Tinubu loves us. It is payback time.” The governor pointed to the ongoing Calabar–Abuja Superhighway (Coastal Road corridor) passing through the state and the construction of a new cement factory as tangible proof of federal backing. “The road to Afikpo is evidence of what the President has done for us. The President is not just constructing roads; he is the brain behind our new cement factory. “That factory is under construction because of him, and he has provided the funds for us to build it. Building industries will lift a lot of our people out of poverty,” the governor said.
